doc.title: Chuck Israels interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 11, 2021

title: Music that assaults the mind: George Winston in restaurants
summary: Rowe reads Israels' quote on numbing music; Israels recalls George Winston's arpeggios in 1970s restaurants.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: You are a poet also. I enjoyed that description. And one more quote I read from you. I think you were addressing music that bothered you. And you said, “Music which assaults the mind and restricts it with a numbing drone commands the brain not to think and holds thought hostage while it rapes the ear.”
Oh boy. I said — that was pretty good. That’s what — I used to think that every — you remember in the 70s when George Winston’s music was ubiquitous?

I’d go into a restaurant and they’d have this Chinese water torture drip of sound of George Winston playing arpeggio triads one after the other after the other after the other. It would drive me right up the wall.
Isn’t it interesting to be sitting in a restaurant like that and thinking am I the only one in here who is driven to distraction by this music?
